title: Tiered Bridge Roles, Scripted Handovers, and Customer Notice Cadence
author: Leila Kapoor
content:
Overview

This page documents the operational model for 'tiered bridge' incident handling at Redwood Inference: a small, script-driven bridge that scales through clear roles and an associated customer notification cadence. The goal is faster containment, consistent customer messaging, and repeatable handovers between shifts and escalation tiers.

Scope

- Applies to Sev-2/Sev-1 incidents affecting production serving, routing, or customer-facing dashboards.
- Not for minor alerts (Sev-3/Sev-4): those follow the lightweight oncall checklist.

Essential principles

1) Minimize cognitive load: bridge scripts must say exactly what to run and what to say.
2) Explicit ownership: every activity has an owner and a follow-up action assigned.
3) Graceful scaling: add tiers (Tier A -> Tier B -> Tier C) only when earlier tiers are exhausted.

Roles and responsibilities (tiered)

- Tier A (Bridge Operator)
  - Primary responsibilities: acknowledge pager within 5 minutes, collect initial signals, execute containment script, start bridge, and publish first customer notice.
  - Typical personnel: SRE on primary rotation.
  - Escalation criteria: SLO breach trending >5% at 10m, inability to apply containment.

- Tier B (Service SME)
  - Primary responsibilities: deep diagnostics, remediation steps for the impacted service, coordinate with infra/serving-runtime teams.
  - Typical personnel: service owner or volunteer SME.
  - Escalation criteria: cross-service impact, dataset or model quality regressions, long-running KV cache corruption.

- Tier C (Incident Commander / Executive Liaison)
  - Primary responsibilities: stakeholder decisions, customer credit/communication approvals, postmortem sign-off and action prioritization.
  - Typical personnel: on-call engineering manager or senior SRE.

Quick reference table

| Role | Who | First action | SLA to respond | Primary artifact |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Tier A | Bridge Operator | Start bridge, capture timeline | 5 minutes | Bridge notes (confluence) |
| Tier B | Service SME | Run diagnostics playbook | 15 minutes | Triage doc, runbook outputs |
| Tier C | Incident Commander | Declare customer impact, approve comms | 30 minutes | Incident timeline & postmortem draft |

Incident lifecycle: step-by-step procedure

1) Alert & Triage (Bridge Operator)
  - Acknowledge pager within 5 minutes.
  - Open the incident bridge using the template: `incident start --service <service> --sev <level> --summary "<one-line>"` (internal CLI).
  - Collect first-10 diagnostics: top-3 symptoms, last deployment id, SLO deviation, noisy errors, region(s) impacted. Use `redwood-cli incident snapshot --last 10m`.

2) Containment (Tier A)
  - Run containment script (if present) from the runbook: `./containment/run-basic-evict.sh --cache kv --region <region>` or trigger a controlled throttle policy.
  - If containment removes customer impact, transition to recovery mode and schedule follow-up.
  - If containment fails or situation degrades, escalate to Tier B.

3) Deep Diagnosis & Remediation (Tier B)
  - SME runs diagnostics checklist in the service runbook (links below). Captures commands and outputs in the bridge notes.
  - Common actions: rollback last deployment, rotate failing worker pool, rehydrate KV caches, increase autoscale target.
  - If a planned hotfix is required, follow the hotfix release SOP (see "rollback-and-hotfix-orchestration-playbook-status-messaging-2024").

4) Customer Impact Declaration (Tier C)
  - If customer-facing SLOs are breached >15 minutes or major customers report errors, Incident Commander must declare impact level.
  - Prepare customer notice using canned templates (section: Customer communication templates).

5) Recovery & Verification
  - Confirm metrics have stabilized to within 90% of the SLO baseline over a 15m window.
  - Run smoke tests: `make smoke-tests SERVICE=<service>`.
  - If verification passes, begin de-escalation and prepare post-incident assignments.

6) Handovers and Closure
  - Before closing, ensure: actions assigned, timelines captured, roll-forward/RCA owners named.
  - Publish customer follow-up (if impacted) and link postmortem draft.
  - Close the bridge only after 2 consecutive verification windows pass and the Incident Commander signs off.

Scripted handover checklist (for shift-to-shift or tier handover)

1) Current state summary (one paragraph).
2) Actions in progress (bullet list with owners and ETA).
3) Outstanding blockers and immediate next steps.
4) Evidence artifacts: links to traces, logs, recent `kubectl` outputs, metric graphs.
4) Explicit handover command: `incident handover --from <user> --to <user> --bridge <id> --summary "<one-line>"`

Playbook examples and commands

- Containment example (cache eviction):
  - `./containment/evict-kv.sh --pool serving-pool-a --pattern "prefix-*" --dry-run`
  - If evict successful: `incident note --bridge <id> --note "Evicted stale keys from pool"`

- Rollback example for service gateway:
  - `deployctl rollback gateway-service --to-revision r2026-11 --reason "rapid error spike"`

On-call rotation guidance and expectations

- Primary objectives: timely acknowledgement, accurate initial triage, and clean bridge operation.
- Acknowledgement target: 5 minutes.
- Average ownership window: 2 hours for Tier A operators before handing to on-call follow-up team.
- Rotation policy: 1 week primary rotation, 2 week secondary; ensure no more than 2 consecutive weeks on primary.

Game day design (quarterly)

Purpose: rehearse bridge mechanics, scripted handovers, and customer comm cadence. Each game day exercises one of: KV cache corruption, burst traffic/noisy neighbor, model quality regression.

Structure:
- 09:00 — Inject simulated alert; Tier A must form bridge within 5 minutes.
- 09:15 — Escalation to Tier B triggered by test scenario.
- 09:45 — Customer notice drafted and approved by Tier C.
- 10:30 — Post-game retro and action assignment.

Scoring rubric:
- Bridge start time (0–10 pts)
- First customer notice accuracy (0–10 pts)
- Handover completeness (0–10 pts)
- Runbook adherence (0–10 pts)

Customer communication templates

- Initial acknowledgement (sent within 30 minutes):
  - Subject: "Redwood service interruption: [<service>] — we are investigating"
  - Body: "We are aware of an issue affecting <service> in <region>. Our on-call team has created an incident bridge and is actively investigating. We will provide a follow-up within 30 minutes with known impact and mitigation steps."

- Status update (every 30–60 minutes until resolved):
  - Short summary of progress, actions taken, and next ETA for update.

- Customer resolution & follow-up:
  - Summary of root cause (plain language), affected customers, timeline, mitigations, and any credits/SLAs applied.

Postmortem template (minimum required sections)

- Title and incident id
- Timeline (minute-level)
- Impact summary (SLOs, customers, regions)
- Root cause and contributing factors
- Corrective actions (owner + ETA)
- Prevention measures and test plan
- Postmortem review sign-offs (Tier C + product liaison)

Governance and SLAs

- Acknowledgement SLA: 5 minutes (target)
- Escalation to Tier B: 15 minutes (target)
- Customer first notice: 30 minutes (target for Sev-1)
- Postmortem published: within 7 business days for Sev-1, 14 business days for Sev-2

Appendices and links

- Service runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index (internal)
- Hotfix and rollback SOP: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rollback-and-hotfix-orchestration-playbook-status-messaging-2024
- Templates: bridge starter template, customer notice templates, postmortem skeleton (attached to this page).

Contact matrix (emergency escalation)

- If unreachable via pager: call escalation list (provided in PagerDuty contact card).
- Legal / PR escalation: contact incident commander; for customer-impacting outages with media coverage, include PR and legal in the bridge within 30 minutes.
